title: Pointers & References
content: Pointer stores a memory address: `int* p = &x;`. Dereference: `*p = 10`. Null pointer: `int* p = nullptr;`. Reference is an alias — must be initialized: `int& r = x; r = 5;` modifies `x`. Pass by pointer: `void fn(int* p)`. Pass by reference: `void fn(int& r)`. Prefer references when the pointer must not be null. `const int* p` = pointer to const value; `int* const p` = const pointer.

title: Heap vs Stack & Manual Memory
content: Stack: automatic, fast, limited (~1MB–8MB). Heap: manual, large, slow. Allocate: `int* p = new int(42);`. Free: `delete p;`. Array: `int* arr = new int[10]; delete[] arr;`. Memory leak: forgetting `delete`. Dangling pointer: using `p` after `delete p`. Modern C++ avoids manual memory with RAII (`unique_ptr`, `shared_ptr`).

title: Smart Pointers (RAII)
content: `unique_ptr<T>` — sole ownership, auto-deleted when out of scope: `auto p = make_unique<Dog>("Rex")`. `shared_ptr<T>` — shared ownership, ref-counted: `auto p = make_shared<Dog>()`. `weak_ptr<T>` — non-owning, breaks circular references. Never mix smart and raw pointers for ownership. Use `std::move` to transfer unique_ptr ownership.

title: STL Containers & Algorithms
content: `vector<int> v = {1,2,3}; v.push_back(4); v.size();`. `map<string,int> m; m["key"]=1; m.count("key");`. `unordered_map` for O(1) average lookup. `set<int>` for sorted unique elements. STL algorithms: `sort(v.begin(), v.end()); auto it = find(v.begin(), v.end(), 3); count_if(v.begin(),v.end(), [](int x){return x>2;});`.

title: Templates (Generic Programming)
content: Function template: `template<typename T> T max(T a, T b){ return a > b ? a : b; }`. Class template: `template<typename T> class Stack { vector<T> data; public: void push(T v){data.push_back(v);} };`. Specialization: `template<> int max<int>(int a,int b){...}`. Template argument deduction: compiler infers `T` from arguments. `constexpr if` for compile-time branching.

title: Move Semantics & Rvalue References
content: Rvalue reference: `int&& r = 42`. Move constructor: `MyClass(MyClass&& other) noexcept { data = other.data; other.data = nullptr; }`. Move assignment: similar. `std::move(x)` casts x to rvalue — enables move instead of copy. `std::forward<T>` for perfect forwarding in templates. Mark move operations `noexcept` for STL compatibility and performance.

title: Lambdas & Closures in C++
content: Syntax: `[capture](params) -> return_type { body }`. Capture by value: `[x]`, by reference: `[&x]`, all by value: `[=]`, all by ref: `[&]`. Example: `auto sq = [](int x){ return x*x; }; sq(5);`. With STL: `sort(v.begin(),v.end(), [](int a,int b){ return a>b; });`. Mutable lambda (modify captured copy): `[x]() mutable { x++; }`.

title: Classes, Inheritance & Virtual Functions
content: Class vs struct: identical except default access (`private` vs `public`). Constructor: `MyClass(int x) : member(x) {}` (initializer list preferred). Destructor: `~MyClass()` — called at end of scope. Virtual function enables runtime polymorphism: `virtual void speak() = 0;` (pure virtual → abstract). Derived must `override`. Always make base destructor `virtual` if class is inherited.

title: Rule of Five (Resource Management)
content: If a class manages a resource (heap memory, file handle), define all five: Destructor, Copy Constructor, Copy Assignment, Move Constructor, Move Assignment. If you don't want copying: `= delete`. If default is fine: `= default`. Modern approach: use RAII wrappers (`unique_ptr`, `vector`) and let the compiler-generated defaults work (Rule of Zero).

title: const & constexpr
content: `const` at runtime: `const int x = 5`. `constexpr` computed at compile time: `constexpr int square(int n){ return n*n; }`. Member function that does not modify state: `int size() const { return n; }`. `mutable` allows a const method to modify a specific field (e.g., cache). Prefer `constexpr` over `#define` for compile-time constants.

title: Namespaces & Scope Resolution
content: Define: `namespace MyLib { void fn(); }`. Call: `MyLib::fn()`. `using namespace std` imports all std symbols (avoid in headers). `using std::cout;` imports just one. Namespace alias: `namespace ml = MyMachineLearningLib;`. Nested: `namespace A::B { }`. Anonymous namespace: `namespace { ... }` — file-internal linkage (like `static`).

title: Exception Handling in C++
content: `try { risky(); } catch(const std::exception& e){ cerr << e.what(); } catch(...){ /* catch-all */ }`. Throw: `throw std::runtime_error("msg")`. Standard exceptions: `std::runtime_error`, `std::invalid_argument`, `std::out_of_range`. `noexcept` guarantees no exception — compiler can optimize. Destructors should never throw. Use RAII to avoid leaks when exceptions propagate.

title: I/O Streams
content: Console: `cout << "Hello " << name << endl;`. `cin >> x;` reads until whitespace. `getline(cin, line)` reads entire line. File read: `ifstream f("file.txt"); string line; while(getline(f,line)){ ... }`. File write: `ofstream out("out.txt"); out << data;`. String stream: `ostringstream oss; oss << x << "," << y; string s = oss.str();`.

title: Complexity Analysis in C++
content: Vector access: O(1). Vector insert at end (amortized): O(1). Insert at middle: O(n). `unordered_map` lookup: O(1) average, O(n) worst. `map` lookup: O(log n). `sort`: O(n log n). Use `reserve(n)` on vectors to avoid reallocations. Prefer `emplace_back` over `push_back` to construct in-place. Profile with `-O2` before optimizing manually.

title: C++ Concurrency (C++11+)
content: `#include <thread>`. Create: `std::thread t(fn, args); t.join();`. Mutex: `std::mutex m; std::lock_guard<mutex> lk(m);`. `std::atomic<int>` for lock-free counters. Async tasks: `auto f = std::async(std::launch::async, fn); auto val = f.get();`. Condition variable: `cv.wait(lk, []{ return ready; }); cv.notify_all();`. Avoid data races — always synchronize shared state.
